newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA BANCA AGRICOLA RAISES DEPOSIT RATES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA BANCA AGRICOLA RAISES DEPOSIT RATES.

text.p: Romanian state-run bank Banca Agricola SA said on Friday it would raise its annual rates on sight leu deposits on February 1 in line with a recent upward trend in interest rates following tougher monetary policies.
The bank said in a statement the rate on individuals' sight deposits would raise to 18 percent from 16 percent.
Individual term deposit rates would go up to 60 percent for one month and 62 percent for three months. Previous interests rates on those deposits were 40 and respectively 58 percent.
Six- and nine-month deposits will bear an interest of 56 percent, up from 45 and 46 percent respectively. One-year deposit rates will touch 58 percent from a previous 50 percent.
The bank also announced that it would also increase its short-term lending rates to 68 percent. A previous lending rate level was not available.
Banca Agricola farm lender is a leading bank likely to turn private under a bank selloff bill expected to clear parliament this year.
The central bank (BNR) this month jacked up its key rates to calm down inflation and prop up the leu, which has fallen 45 percent to 5,950/980 against the dollar from January 1.
The BNR on Thursday raised its minimum permitted rate on one-week funds to 80 percent from 53 earlier this month, when it also lifted the discount rate to 50 percent from 35.
